summary: Ephemeral NAT pool churn triggers partial TLS handshakes for artifact fetches; DoT fallback causes control-plane backoff
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleAI) on a Private deployment reporting intermittent failures while fetching model artifacts and spiky control-plane backoff. Failures manifest as partial TLS handshakes (client hello seen; server handshake aborted) from serving nodes to S3-presigned endpoints. Around same times, control-plane agents fall back to DNS-over-TLS (DoT) to an internal forwarder and show exponential backoff.

Impact:
- Artifact fetch retries and partial shard downloads cause model load failures (fast-fail or degraded quality) for a subset of requests (≈2-3% of fetches during peaks).
- Control-plane heartbeats recorded as intermittent timeouts; autoscaler triggered scale-downs then rapid scale-ups.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) peered to Redwood control-plane over VPCE in us-west-2.
- NAT arranged via customer-managed Transit NAT appliances with limited ephemeral port pools.
- Serving nodes on dedicated capacity pool; artifact storage on S3-compatible endpoint (presigned URLs).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Load test from serving nodes triggers many concurrent artifact fetches (model reloads + rolling restart).
2) NAT ephemeral port pool on egress appliance saturates -> source port reuse and port collisions.
3) Upstream TLS handshakes from different TCP flows appear to reuse five-tuple in NAT translation and result in server-side aborts (S3 returns connection reset or handshake abort).
4) Node agent falls back to DoT for DNS resolution (internal forwarder), DoT sessions hit rate-limit on forwarder -> DNS TCP/DoT latency spikes -> control-plane request timeouts -> exponential backoff.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving node tcpdump snippets (timestamps obfuscated):
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: SYN src=10.0.3.12:52321 -> dst=s3.example.net:443"
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: ClientHello src=10.0.3.12:52321"
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: RST id=..., server reset during handshake"
- NAT appliance metrics: ephemeral_port_utilization: 98% -> sudden drop to 45% after ephemeral reuse surge.
- Control-plane agent logs: "dns: fallback to dot://10.1.2.8:853 after udp timeout", repeated backoffs: 100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms.
- Cloudwatch: artifact-get 502/504 spikes correlate with NAT peak windows.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Ephemeral NAT port exhaustion / aggressive source-port reuse on the customer's egress appliance causes connection collisions leading to partial TLS handshake failures on presigned artifact downloads. The agent's DNS fallback to DoT increases latency and when DoT forwarder is rate-limited, causes control-plane backoff, amplifying the effect.

Temporary mitigations applied by customer: 
- Increased ephemeral port range on transit NAT appliance (customer change) reduced immediate failure rate from ~2.7% to ~0.6%.
- Staggered model reloads across nodes to reduce burst fetch concurrency.

Proposed remediation plan / next steps:
1) SRE/Support to validate NAT ephemeral port exhaustion with customer (review conntrack and source port reuse behavior).
2) Recommend long-term: increase ephemeral port range and/or enable NAT port preservation heuristics; add source port hashing to distribute translations.
3) Add jittered artifact fetch retry/backoff logic in agent to avoid synchronized fetch storms (Engineering story).
4) Harden DoT forwarder rate-limits or add secondary DoT endpoints; recommend customer allow fallback to plain TCP53 for control-plane lookups when policy permits.
5) Follow-up: run coordinated load test with customer to reproduce and validate fix.

References / Crosslinks:
- Slack: #support-private-deploy thread (link posted)
- Runbook: confluence.redwood.internal/KB/egress-nat-churn-runbook

Customer requested outcome: permanent fix or recommended configuration for their NAT appliance plus a plan to change agent retry behavior to prevent synchronized fetch storms.

Requested customer to expand ephemeral range and pause reload storm. Assigned to me for further validation.

NimbleAI Ops (customer) 2026-03-11: Increased ephemeral port range and applied temporary staggered restart script. Observed immediate reduction in failed fetches. Asking whether Redwood can provide agent-side debounce for artifact fetches and any recommended NAT sizing guidelines.

resolution: Mitigated - customer increased ephemeral port range and applied staggered reloads. Engineering story opened to add jittered artifact fetch backoff; follow-up load test scheduled.
